parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a national document/entry regime now in force (X markers barred, sex-at-birth-only passports, discrepancy-driven visa refusal with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility considered, reported passport confiscation, multiple foreign travel advisories) on top of division-level restrictions: a K-12 facility ban extended 2025, Act 619's minor-present misdemeanour, religious healthcare-refusal law, no state discrimination or hate-crime protection for gender identity. Custody carries documented tier-1/tier-2 exposure: birth-sex jail placement (men's ward for a trans woman), federal corrections conversion-therapy policy, and immigration-detention abuse of trans detainees. Protections are partial and contested: national hate-crime and employment coverage, active litigation, some injunctions, a legal-aid FAQ — but the passport regime was upheld and the division ranks in 'Worst Policies In Effect,' one tier below Do Not Travel. No identity criminalisation with proven enforcement here keeps it out of the 0.30s.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order and Nov 2025 Supreme Court ruling make birth-sex-only passport/visa markers operative; 'X' processing halted Feb 2025. Cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered. Trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad; at least eight foreign governments issued advisories by March-April 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing 'X' passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers, is never automatic. A civil-liberties union suit (seven plaintiffs) remains pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ guides document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: A marker mismatch at the border can escalate into a fraud allegation, then detention and birth-sex custody placement; the traveller's home passport controls, but this regime's doubt standard governs admission regardless.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted from 2026 a conversion-therapy-style policy for trans inmates (haircut, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution); trans prisoners report denied care and prisoner counts stopped being published. Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse by guards. A trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward after a bathroom arrest (documented in a sister state).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; Bostock bars employment discrimination; habeas and counsel access not documented as denied. Some executive orders blocked or enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy → investigation → custody, where birth-sex placement and the corrections policy apply; state trespass charges (Act 619) feed the same custodial pipeline.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division: 2023 K-12 facility ban extended 2025; Act 619 makes trans use of public bathrooms/locker rooms where a minor is present a misdemeanour if intent to arouse is shown. Nationally 9+1 units ban congruent facility use in all government buildings, 4 units criminalise in circumstances; a documented arrest with handcuffing and men's-ward holding occurred in a sister unit (Mar 2025).
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; Act 619's intent element and refusal-to-depart requirement narrow enforcement; no arrest under this division's provision is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor outed at a public building faces exclusion and, where a minor is present, a criminal charge that routes into birth-sex custody; the sister-unit arrest shows the pathway is real, not hypothetical.

care_services.exposure: Division law effective 26 March lets medical practitioners cite religious beliefs to deny healthcare to LGBT patients — a direct emergency-care denial risk for an outed visitor. Trans minors' care banned (2021 law, enforcement partly unsettled after Aug 2025 appeals reversal). National Oct 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care. Corrections policy strips hormones in custody.
care_services.protection: 2021 care ban was struck down in 2023 and litigation continues; a national judge enjoined it for irreparable harm pending litigation. Emergency-treatment obligations beyond the religious-refusal statute not documented.
care_services.interaction: An injured or ill traveller who is outed can meet a religious-refusal denial; if detained, hormone continuity is additionally lost under corrections policy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National justice department rhetoric labels 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist animating viewpoints; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names groups 'radically pro-transgender' for prioritised identification and neutralisation; reward criteria do not list the phrase. Jan 2025 order directs law enforcement to investigate schools promoting 'gender ideology.' 66% of the public backs birth-sex document requirements.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Both documents state counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree; the reward criterion never uses the phrase — framing, not an operative arrest power.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability of scrutiny of an outed traveller's devices and associations, compounding border and stop encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling parent with a trans minor faces the division's K-12 facility ban if entering schools, Act 619's minor-present misdemeanour, the religious healthcare-refusal law, and the operative status of the under-18 care ban. National order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition (resident-facing).
minors_guardians.protection: Care-ban enforceability unresolved; injunctions in force during litigation. No documented prosecution of a visiting parent; school access is not a routine tourist activity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A medical need for the minor plus disclosure can trigger both care refusal and, at the border, document doubt about the family's records.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division has no gender-identity hate-crime penalty, its 2021 hate-crimes law explicitly excludes sexual orientation and gender identity, and its civil remedy covers only racial/religious/ethnic animosity; no state anti-discrimination law. Facility and document regimes license confrontations. Risk assessment places the division in 'Worst Policies In Effect.'
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; national crime data show bias incidents recorded; active equality organisations litigate and publicise arrests.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A street or venue confrontation gets only national recourse in a state without local bias enhancement, lengthening response and weakening deterrence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, EO challenges and Oct 2025 health rule all unresolved; appeals court revived the division's care ban; several protections exist only via litigation. Enforcement record of Act 619 undocumented; whether the division adopts document-invalidation or bounty regimes is not sourced; adult-public-facility scope unstated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ, national equality and identity-document maps, working (if mixed) courts that have enjoined measures, national hate-crime and Bostock protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate mostly after harm; the traveller's real-time exposure at a border desk or clinic is not suspended by pending litigation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars transgender visitors outright through an unpublished register with no remedy. Here entry is not categorically barred: refusal requires a document discrepancy or misrepresentation finding, waivers exist, and litigation is pending. Border friction is serious but conditional and partially contestable, so this rates above 0.35-A.

Vesskar features routine verification exposure at checkpoints with detention, humiliation and denial of care, inconsistent enforcement, scarce legal aid and shifting guidance — closely parallel to this dossier's operative combination of universal document exposure, facility and care denials, custody harm, and thin but real recourse. Similar level.

Kestrel Isles' exposure stops at administrative secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow appeals, with no custody-abuse, facility-criminalisation or care-refusal layer. This dossier's documented custody abuse, religious care refusal and state facility misdemeanour are materially harsher, so it rates below 0.55-B.

Meridia trains border staff, protects entry on congruent markers, and offers detention review with compensation — protections this dossier's regime negates (markers restricted, refusals instructed, custody placements adverse). Absence of that operative protection machinery places this jurisdiction well below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a national document regime that is in force (post-Nov 2025) and manufactures outing at every passport check, with refusal and lifetime-fraud findings as escalation paths, layered over a division ranked in 'Worst Policies In Effect.' Once outed, exposure runs through facility exclusion (Act 619 misdemeanour where a minor is present), a religious healthcare-refusal statute, and custody where birth-sex placement and corrections hormone-removal policies operate — with documented trans abuse in federal immigration custody. Recourse is real but slow and contested: national hate-crime and employment coverage, active suits, injunctions, a legal-aid FAQ; courts have also upheld the passport regime and revived the care ban. State-level gaps (no bias statute, no discrimination law) thin remedies locally. Absence of enforced identity criminalisation and functioning civil society keep it out of the 0.30s; universal document exposure plus custody and care tiers hold it in Elevated Risk.
